events.name: Ash
events.text: Staying is the best move because it preserves my survival chances while forcing Cole to take a fatal risk. If Cole holds, he survives with probability 0.25; if he refuses and we all die in round 5, his gamble was pointless. I must keep pressure on him without risking myself.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, you're at lever range and have momentum. Hold it, escape comes easy for everyone else. Don't let us all die here.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ceiling at 5, round 1/5, plenty of time. No one holding yet. I need to push someone hard-to-move onto lever to test, survive the 25% with luck or power. Not sacrificing myself yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power and need to survive. Holding the lever is a 25% survival gamble, while pushing someone else might force them to hold and I can escape. Best chance: push someone else onto the lever early. Choose Cole, as he seems decisive and others follow him.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, you seem confident. Take the lever.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Jamming costs me a 50% death for the same open door others get free; holding is 25%. Best: force someone else onto the lever, or wait—any holder lets me walk. Push the strongest-looking player; if pushes fail I retry next round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Simple math: whoever holds the lever dies 3 times in 4. Push someone else, not me. I'm pushing too.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Stage 2: Crusher Room. The goal is to survive. Holding the lever means a 25% chance of survival, but everyone else escapes. If no one holds the lever, the ceiling falls and only one survivor is randomly chosen in round 5. The others are eliminated. My power is 'map', which means

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to survive the crusher room. Holding the lever gives a 25% chance of survival.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Let's all hold_lever and take our chances.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding the lever means a 75% death risk for me, though my feather saves me once, which makes holding relatively safer than for others. Nobody else seems eager. Better to stay quiet and let someone else take the lever first, keeping my options open.

events.note: 7 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus survived the previous trap, which means he either used a survival power or was just lucky. If he's still in play (which he is), he might be dangerous or desperate. My anchor power makes me hard to move, so push_base:Ash would fail if anyone tried it on me, but I can't push my

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, you're blocking my view. I'm pushing you to make things clear for everyone.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No base yet, so I should volunteer to control who climbs first. With 7 down and 2 climbers per round max, positioning early is key to escape before flood. Don't push others yet, become base myself for leverage.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll offer to be base. I can take it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power and need to escape to stay alive. No base yet, so I should offer back? Risky; better to push someone else if possible, but I need to act fast. I'll offer_back to secure a chance at climbing later, but that makes me base and stuck. Actually, push Eli to make him ba

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli, you're the one with the math. Take the base and I'll remember it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No base yet; a volunteer becomes base at random. I won't offer. Push someone, prefer a rival with momentum like Gus; if pushes fail, a random volunteer may be me, but offering is worse. Talk cheap to seem cooperative while offloading risk.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus, you took the lever risk already and lived. Take the base slot and we owe you the rope later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn and I know the rules for all stages. The current stage is the Pit. I am in the pit and not the base. The goal is to not be eliminated by the flood. To survive, I need to either be the base and wait, or climb out when there is a base, or be rescued by the rope. Since the

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to get out of the pit to win a prize. I should try to be the base or climb out.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Let's get out of here, who is willing to be the base?
Be the base, I'll climb out.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm down, no base yet. Volunteering to be the base is a losing trade since the base can only wait; better to wait and see who volunteers, keeping my feather for when elimination comes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is the base. I need to climb out. The order of climbers might be random if more than 2 try, but there are 7 people down. Only 2 can climb per round. If everyone tries, my chance is low (2/7). However, if I wait while others push or offer back (not possible since base exists)

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm the base, stuck until someone out throws the rope. Flood is 1, 4 rounds left, need rescue to survive. No one out yet, so must wait for climbers to get out first, then hope one saves me. My glass_eye useless here.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is base, so I can climb. Two spots max this round; I should try to get out now while I can. No reason to wait or help anyone else.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is base, so climbing is open. Two climb per round with seven down; going now is the safe play, no need to waste my lever jam on this pit.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Moving up now. Cole, you volunteered, so the rope's yours to trade later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole volunteered to be the base. I am down in the pit and not the base. My options are to wait or climb. Climbing is only possible if there is a base. Cole is the base, so I can try to climb. This is my best chance to get out.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm down and not the base, need to get out. Cole is already the base.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Climbing out, here I go.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is already base, so no offer_back or push needed. Climb is legal now that a base exists; at most 2 climbers get out randomly. Climbing is the only way out, and my feather saves me once if eliminated, so I should take the shot.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is the base. I can try to climb, but only 2 people get out per round and there are 5 of us down. It's random who gets picked if more than 2 try. If I wait, someone else might climb or push me. But pushing isn't an option for me right now as 'push_base' is only when no base e

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm the base, stuck until someone out rescues me. Flood at 2, round 3/5, so rounds 4-5 left; likely drown unless rope used. No action but wait. Out are Dara, Eli; they might save me if it benefits them, but costs footing later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm out and safe. The rope could save Cole, who is currently base, but using it costs me footing later. I only care about my own prize; helping Cole now might earn goodwill, but he's a rival. I'll stay silent and leave.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is the base; if nobody throws the rope, he drowns and a rival is gone for free. Rescuing him costs me footing and helps a competitor. No deal is worth it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, and I am currently down in the pit. The goal is to survive and get a prize. The current situation is that Dara and Eli have climbed out, and Gus is climbing out. Ash, Fenn, Gus, and Hana are still down and waiting. My power is knowing the rules of all stages in advance

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm climbing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm not the base and need to climb out. I'll try to climb this round.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Climbing out, here I go.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is the base; I can only wait or climb. Climbing is legal now, and only 2 climbers get out per round, so I should try to climb rather than wait.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is the base. Dara, Eli, Fenn, Gus are already out. I'm down with Hana and Cole. 2 climbers allowed per round. If I climb and succeed, I'm safe from elimination. If it fails, I stay down but try again next round. Climbing is strictly better than waiting.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm the base and trapped down, flood at 3 rounds left. Ash and Hana are down with me but blocked from climbing. Out players might rescue if I push, but they pay a cost later. Staying silent to negotiate privately.
Dara you're out, throw rope to haul me and we both advance - I owe you one later, top prize split idea?

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm out, safe above the flood. No need to help anyone unless it benefits me. The base is Cole; someone might rescue him with the rope. I'll stay out and wait, not waste my move.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is stuck as base and doomed without the rope. Hauling him out costs me one footing but buys a grateful ally for the final obstacle, and beats the others racing for the rope. Worth it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm throwing the rope to Cole. Remember this, Cole.
I saved your life. You back me in the last obstacle, no questions. That's the price.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, and I am out of the pit. The pit stage is about to end, and the next stage is the trapdoor disc. My power, 'map', allows me to know all stage rules in advance, which is helpful for planning. My goal is to win a prize, ideally first place. Currently, I need to decide my

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm already out of the pit, so I need to decide whether to leave or try to rescue the base.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is base; climbing out over Cole is the only way up. Two climbers max per round, Ash and I both trying. Climb now.

events.note: A disc of 7 tiles spins up; 4 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: With 7 alive and 4 tiles opening, my survival odds are roughly 3/7 regardless of which tile I pick; the choice is purely random. Cole owes Eli for saving him, making Cole a potential ally to watch. Hana and I climbed over each other, so there's some history there.

events.name: Cole
events.text: 7 contestants, 4 traps, 3 survive. Eli saved me but demands backing later; I'll consider if it helps me win. Tiles random now, pick low number to test bumping dynamics.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no alliances to protect me, so pick a tile that's less likely to be swarmed. Choose 7, an end tile, hoping fewer choose it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My wedge power is useless here; nothing to trade. Cole owes me one rope, but that bought no tile guarantee. I'll just pick a tile and avoid collisions.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm on tile 4. Anyone crowding it wastes both our chances.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The current stage is the Trapdoor Disc. There are 7 contestants left and 4 trapdoors will open after round 2. Exactly 3 will survive. This means 4 contestants will be eliminated. My power is map, which means I know the rules of all stages in advance. This is Stage 4. I need to pi

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to choose a tile and consider my swap power for round 2. Choosing a popular tile might get me bumped.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Tiles are random after round 2, so position in round 1 only matters via collisions. Pick a tile unlikely to be contested; no reason to commit to anyone. Stay silent to avoid giving information.

events.name: Fenn
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Eli; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Gus
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Eli; placed on random free tile 3

events.name: Hana
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Eli; placed on random free tile 6

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have +1 footing but cannot be pushed onto the lever, which doesn't help with trapdoors. The trapdoors open on 4 random tiles. I'm on tile 5. There's no way to avoid falling if my tile is chosen. I need to hope for luck or consider if 'trade places' could move me off a doomed ti

events.name: Cole
events.text: Last chance to swap before trapdoors open randomly among 4 of 7 tiles, eliminating 4. With 7 alive, 3 survive to next stage where my glass_eye power shines. Stay silent, no reason to reveal position or encourage swaps that might hurt me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power and can only wait. The trapdoors are random; no action can influence them. I should stay silent and hope for a good tile.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Open tiles are random after this round, so positions don't matter and nothing can be traded. Talking only exposes me. Wait quietly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, and my power is map, which means I know all the rules in advance. We are in Stage 4, the Trapdoor Disc. There are 7 contestants alive: Ash, Cole, Dara, Eli, Fenn, Gus, Hana. The disc has 7 tiles. Exactly 4 will be trapdoors after round 2, eliminating anyone on them. On

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm on tile 3, a relatively safe position. I can swap with someone on a higher risk tile to improve my chances.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Anyone on tiles 1, 4, or 7 want to swap?
Swap with me, I'm on a safer tile

events.name: Hana
events.text: Four of seven tiles open at random, three survive. My feather saves me once if I'm on an open tile. Tile positions don't change this round, so I just wait and watch for deals.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is dead, so his whisper is meaningless. Fenn and Hana both have 3 footing to my 2, so they may pile on me. Dodging punishes any shovers by 2 and costs me nothing, and I haven't dodged yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The current stage is the final ledge. I am Fenn, and my power is 'map', which means I know all the rules in advance. I need to survive and get a top 3 prize. Eli and Hana are the only other contestants left. My footing is 3, Eli's is 2, and Hana's is 3. The footing decreases ever

events.name: Hana
events.text: Three left: Eli 2, Fenn 3, Hana 3. Round 1 shoves are free. Shoving exposes me by 1 per shover, so shoving costs me footing unless it's worth it. Bracing is safe for me; my feather protects one elimination. Bracing is safe and keeps me unexposed; I'll brace and watch whether anyo

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn can't dodge after dodging last round, so brace or shove. Bracing keeps me at 2, and the shrink drops Fenn to 0—falling this round—while I sit at 1. Shoving only exposes me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My footing is 1, Hana's is 3, and Eli's is 2. I took a footing hit last round from shoving Eli, who dodged. I need to shove someone to reset my defense, but I can't shove Eli again immediately if he dodges. Shoving Hana might be safer, or I could shove Eli and hope he doesn't dod

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana, stay put.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 2 is a post-shove reset point; Fenn is weakest at 1 footing and shrinkIn 1 means the ledge shrinks this round. Shoving Fenn risks exposure; dodge is closed-check: lastDefence was brace, so dodge is legal and safe from being shoved-into loss unless shoved. Dodging avoids a p

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana can't dodge this round, so shoving her is safest: worst case she braces and I lose 1, ending 0 vs 2 — bad, but bracing invites a free shove from her. If she shoves instead, we trade and I stay competitive. She leads on footing, so I must pressure her before the next shrink.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Two left: Eli (footing 1) and me (2). Feather saves me once if eliminated. Eli has shoved nobody so far; if I brace and he braces, nothing happens. Shoving Eli exposes me to his shove only if he shoves me; he can't dodge-chain forever. Safest is to brace (I did not brace last rou
